title: 卜算子·黄州定慧院寓居作
titlePy: Bǔ Suàn Zǐ · Huángzhōu Dìnghuì Yuàn Yùjū Zuò
titleEn: Song of Divination: Written While Lodging at Dinghui Temple, Huangzhou
author: 苏轼
intro: Fresh from prison and newly exiled, Su Shi walks alone under a broken moon and sees a lone wild goose that will not settle on any cold branch. One of the loneliest poems in Chinese — and one of the proudest.
analysis: 这首词是苏轼刚到黄州、住在定慧院时写的。上阕写夜景：一弯残缺的月亮挂在稀疏的梧桐树上，漏壶的水滴完了，夜深人静。谁看见一个幽居的人独自走来走去？只有那隐隐约约的孤雁的影子。“幽人”是诗人自己，“孤鸿”也是诗人自己——人和雁在月下合成了一个孤独的形象。下阕专写孤鸿：它突然受惊飞起，又回过头来，心里有怨恨却没有人理解；它把寒冷的树枝都挑遍了，也不肯落在上面，宁愿待在寂寞冰冷的沙洲上。这里用了托物言志的手法——借写一样东西来表达自己的志向：孤鸿受了惊、无人理解，还不肯随便栖身，正像苏轼经历“乌台诗案”后的处境——心有余悸，孤独无助，却依然清高，不愿随波逐流。
analysisEn: Su Shi wrote this soon after arriving in Huangzhou, while staying at Dinghui Temple. The first half sets a night scene: a broken moon hangs in a bare wutong tree; the water clock has run dry, and the world is asleep. Who sees the recluse pacing back and forth alone? Only the faint shadow of a lone wild goose. The “recluse” is the poet, and the goose is the poet too — under the moon, man and bird blur into a single lonely figure. The second half is all about the goose. Startled, it takes off, then turns its head back; it carries a hurt that no one understands. It tries every cold branch and refuses to perch on any, settling instead on a lonely, freezing sandbar. This technique is called tuō wù yán zhì — speaking of your own ideals through an object. The goose, frightened and misunderstood but still too proud to roost just anywhere, is Su Shi after the Crow Terrace trial: shaken, isolated, and yet unwilling to bend to fit in. The word 省 (“to understand”) is pronounced xǐng here — a good one to remember.
background: Su Shi (1037–1101) was jailed for over four months in 1079 for poems said to criticize the government, and only narrowly escaped death. Sent to Huangzhou in 1080, he lodged at first in Dinghui Temple, where this was written, probably in 1080–1082.
pronunciation: 疏 shū；缥缈 piāo miǎo；省 xǐng（明白、理解，不读 shěng）；拣 jiǎn；栖 qī。
version: 采用通行版本。“谁见幽人独往来”一作“时见幽人独往来”（维基文库等古本多作“时见”）。题目一作“黄州定惠院寓居作”。

lines.zh: 缺月挂疏桐，漏断人初静。
lines.rhythm: 缺月/挂疏桐，漏断/人初静
lines.py: quē yuè guà shū tóng, lòu duàn rén chū jìng
lines.lit: A broken moon hangs on the sparse wutong; the water clock runs out, people first fall still.
lines.en: A broken moon caught in the bare wutong; the water clock has stopped, the world gone quiet.

lines.zh: 谁见幽人独往来，缥缈孤鸿影。
lines.rhythm: 谁见/幽人/独往来，缥缈/孤鸿影
lines.py: shuí jiàn yōu rén dú wǎng lái, piāo miǎo gū hóng yǐng
lines.lit: Who sees the hermit going back and forth alone? Faint and far, a lone goose’s shadow.
lines.en: Who sees the recluse pacing alone? Only a lone goose, a faint shadow overhead.

lines.zh: 惊起却回头，有恨无人省。
lines.rhythm: 惊起/却回头，有恨/无人省
lines.py: jīng qǐ què huí tóu, yǒu hèn wú rén xǐng
lines.lit: Startled up, it turns its head back; it has a grief no one understands.
lines.en: Startled, it rises, then looks back — its hurt understood by no one.
lines.tts: 惊起却回头，有恨无人醒。

lines.zh: 拣尽寒枝不肯栖，寂寞沙洲冷。
lines.rhythm: 拣尽/寒枝/不肯栖，寂寞/沙洲冷
lines.py: jiǎn jìn hán zhī bù kěn qī, jì mò shā zhōu lěng
lines.lit: Picking through all the cold branches, it will not perch; lonely, the sandbar is cold.
lines.en: It tries every cold branch and will settle on none — the sandbar is lonely and cold.

words.note: 不圆的月亮，现代汉语说“残月”。

words.en: a wutong tree with sparse leaves
the water clock has run out — deep night
words.note: 漏：古代滴水计时的漏壶。
现代汉语也说，如“虚无缥缈”。
古义多指遗憾、愁怨；现代汉语“恨”多指“恨某人”，意思更重。
读 xǐng，如“反省”“不省人事”；“省钱”的“省”读 shěng。
江河中由泥沙堆成的小块陆地。

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 残缺的月亮营造冷清的深夜，也暗示诗人心境的残缺。
imagery.en: The broken moon makes the night bleak and hints at the poet’s broken spirits.

imagery.name: 梧桐
imagery.zh: 叶子稀疏的梧桐写出秋夜的萧条冷落。
imagery.en: A thinly leaved wutong tree adds to the bare, cheerless autumn night.

imagery.name: 雁
imagery.zh: 孤鸿就是诗人自己：受惊、孤独、无人理解，却不肯随便栖身。
imagery.en: The lone goose is the poet himself — frightened, alone, misunderstood, yet too proud to perch just anywhere.
